classification.difficultyReason: Two factor-theorem checks are followed by finding the third factor from the leading and constant terms, as the question directs. This is a short, signposted chain of routine steps, comparable to p66-q14.

content.prompt: Show that $P(x)=2x^3-7x^2-17x+10$ is divisible by both $(x+2)$ and $(x-5)$. By considering the leading term and constant term, express $P(x)$ as a product of three linear factors and hence solve $P(x)=0$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P(-2)&=2(-2)^3-7(-2)^2-17(-2)+10\\&=-16-28+34+10\\&=0\\P(5)&=2(5)^3-7(5)^2-17(5)+10\\&=250-175-85+10\\&=0\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $(x+2)$ and $(x-5)$ are factors of $P(x)$.
Write $P(x)=(x+2)(x-5)(ax+b)$.
The leading coefficient gives
$$a=2.$$
The constant term gives
$$\begin{align*}(2)(-5)b&=10\\b&=-1\end{align*}$$
Thus
$$P(x)=(x+2)(x-5)(2x-1).$$
By the null factor law, $x=-2,\ 5,\ \frac12$.
